lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 34

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Woman He Chose
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor was a lung.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It contracted and expanded around them with a slow, rhythmic wheeze of stone. Dust drifted from the ceiling in thin gray threads, caught and released with each breath the passage took. The oily stone sweated moisture that smelled of copper and wet earth, and beneath that something colder—the smell of anything in this place that had decided to remember them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek walked with one hand resting on his satchel.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal no longer felt like a book. It felt like a hook set somewhere behind his ribs, its weight tugging with every step. Every step reminded him of the price he had paid to keep NEEN-soon real. Every step also reminded him that the reason for that price was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had always believed that understanding a price preserved some ownership over the transaction. He had traded sleep for profit, honesty for the Collector's coin, comfort for survival. The City had shown him the flaw in that belief. It took the receipt along with the goods.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind him, NEEN-soon kept pace.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her footsteps were light against the stone. For the first hour after the corridor swallowed the previous chamber he had kept expecting them to disappear—for the rhythm behind him simply to stop, the way a heartbeat stops, without announcement. He kept expecting her shape to blur, her name to slip through his fingers the way water slips through a cracked jar.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She was still there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He knew her name–NEEN-soon. Nothing followed the name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He could remember the payment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He no longer remembered why.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg walked ahead, axe resting across his shoulders, the pack heavy on his back. Whatever had knocked from inside it had remained quiet since the fourth strike. He had not opened the straps. Curiosity, they had learned, was often a form of consent.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo kept to the side, the golden figurine still in her possession. She simply carried it, as though carrying it had become part of a route whose purpose belonged to someone else.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor narrowed without warning.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The walls pressed close enough that Zeek's shoulders brushed both sides. Looking back had begun to feel like asking a question the City might answer with a cost. He did not look back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: After a time the walls eased. The corridor opened into a wider section scored with shallow parallel grooves, as though something large had been dragged through it more than once. The air grew colder. The copper smell thickened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon spoke for the first time since they had left the ledger chamber.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You don't remember why.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was not a question.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: But you remember that you chose.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A longer silence. Then:
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Does that still count?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not answer immediately. Some questions were themselves transactions.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It counts to me,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said at last.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He was not sure whether that was true.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon did not press. She walked a few paces farther and then said, almost to herself,
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The tablets never mentioned this part. The part where you keep the person and lose the reason.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg glanced back once.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You two finished? The floor ahead looks wrong.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek tested it out of habit. His body still knew the sequence even if the conscious lesson was gone. The stone held. They continued.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor began to slope more steeply. At one point the torch caught a pale scar in the limestone—the ghost of a name crossed out so thoroughly only the shape of the erasure remained. He did not stop to read it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind him NEEN-soon's breathing stayed steady. He counted it without meaning to: the quiet intake, the quieter release. As long as he could hear it, the payment was still holding.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not know how long payments held in this place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not know whether the City considered the transaction closed or merely deferred.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor turned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ahead the stone opened into a chamber whose far wall was lost in shadow. The air moved differently here—not the breathing of the passage, but a slow circulation that seemed to come from below the floor itself. Four shallow depressions marked the threshold, each the size of a kneeling figure. A fifth depression sat slightly apart, empty and darker than the rest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stopped.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: This is new.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo tilted her head, studying the darkness.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Or very old.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon came up beside Zeek. She did not touch him. She simply stood close enough that he could feel the fact of her presence without needing the memory of its value.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You chose me,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said quietly. Not accusing. Not grateful. Stating the remaining fact.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I did.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Even without the reason.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Even without the reason.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She was silent a moment. Then:
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The City will not stop at one payment. You know that.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: When it asks again, what will you give it?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked into the dark beyond the chamber's edge. The mark under the linen on his palm was warm, patient, waiting.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They stood in silence while the City breathed around them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then Zeek stepped into the dark, listening for NEEN-soon's next breath.
